claim: Mass cytometry is a cutting-edge high-dimensional technology for profiling marker expression at the single-cell level.

claim: The vast data generated by CyTOF poses a significant analytical challenge.

claim: The ImmCellTyper workflow includes five key steps: batch effect evaluation and correction, data quality control and pre-processing, main cell lineage characterisation and quantification, in-depth investigation of specific cell types, and differential analysis.
source: The workflow includes five key steps: (1) batch effect evaluation and correction, (2) data quality control and pre-processing, (3) main cell lineage characterisation and quantification, (4) in-depth investigation of specific cell types; and (5) differential analysis of cell abundance and functional marker expression across study groups.

claim: Mass cytometry employs stable elemental isotopes to detect cellular proteins of interest.
source: Mass cytometry or cytometry by time-of-flight (CyTOF) is a powerful high-throughput single-cell technology which employs stable elemental isotopes, as the same manner of fluorophores, to detect cellular proteins of interest.
evidence: This describes the technical principle of mass cytometry based on established knowledge.

claim: CyTOF permits simultaneous measurement of over 40 parameters on millions of cells.
source: This approach successfully tackles the panel multiplex challenges faced by traditional flow cytometry due to spectral overlap and permits simultaneous measurement of over 40 parameters on millions of cells.
evidence: This statement describes the technical capability of CyTOF technology based on established knowledge.

claim: CyTOF has been widely applied in basic and translational medical research including deep immunophenotyping, immune monitoring of cell-adoptive therapy, and dissecting cell subpopulations from heterogeneous tumour samples.
source: To date, CyTOF has been widely applied in basic and translational medical research, such as deep immunophenotyping and characterisation of novel refined cell subsets, immune monitoring of cell-adoptive therapy, and dissecting cell subpopulations from heterogeneous tumour samples (Spitzer and Nolan, 2016).

claim: Traditional gating strategy for flow cytometry serves as the 'gold standard' for cell population identification in cytometry data.
source: Traditional gating strategy for flow cytometry, while still serving as the 'gold standard' for cell population identification in cytometry data, may not be an optimal option for CyTOF data due to its high-dimensional settings.

claim: Manual gating is extremely labour intensive and time-consuming for CyTOF data due to high-dimensional settings.
source: The high-parametric resolution in CyTOF, aimed at revealing previously undiscovered cell subpopulations, leads to a significant increase in the complexity of gating schemas and hierarchical depth, which makes manual gating extremely labour intensive and time-consuming (Kimball et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Unsupervised clustering methods include flowSOM, Phenograph, X-shift, spade, and DensVM.
